title: Electrophysiological correlates of emotion processing in schizophrenia: a systematic review and meta-analysis of P300 event-related potentials
abstract: Abstract Introduction: Schizophrenia is characterized by deficits in social cognition, including impaired facial emotion recognition (FER). The P300 event-related potential (ERP) indexes attention and context updating and is reduced in schizophrenia. Whether this reduction varies by facial-emotion valence is unclear. We quantified valence-specific P300 differences, comparing adults with schizophrenia and healthy controls across explicit FER and implicit facial emotion processing (iFEP) tasks. Methods: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis following PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, Web of Science, and SCOPUS were searched through May 2025. Studies were included if they reported P300 responses to positive or negative facial expressions. Results: Ten studies met the inclusion criteria; six were eligible for meta-analysis. In response to positive facial expressions (k=5; n=237), P300 amplitude was significantly reduced in schizophrenia (Hedges’ g=−0.40, 95%CI [−0.59,−0.21], p<0.001). For negative expressions (k=6; n=281), a smaller, marginally significant reduction was observed (Hedges’ g=−0.31, 95%CI [−0.62,0.00], p=0.05). One iFEP study found no differences. Conclusions: Results suggest valence-specific P300 attenuation during emotion processing in schizophrenia, particularly for positive expressions, potentially reflecting impaired salience attribution. P300 may represent a candidate electrophysiological, temporally resolved ERP biomarker for impaired social-affective processing and a candidate endpoint for cognitive remediation studies.
